a-modern-utopia: H. G. Wells blends fiction and philosophy in this bold thought experiment: what would a truly well-run world look like? Two travelers visit a planet-wide utopia and debate its laws, customs, and freedoms with their hosts. Part novel, part political essay, the book lays out Wells's hopeful — and sometimes unsettling — vision of a rational future society.
old-mission-stories-of-california: Charles Franklin Carter gathers legends and true tales from California's old Spanish missions — San Juan Capistrano, Santa Barbara, and their sisters. Padres, Indians, and pioneers people stories of faith, hardship, and romance in the days of New Spain. The collection preserves the colorful lore of California's mission era for modern readers.
queen-lucia: E. F. Benson introduces Lucia Lucas — Queen Lucia — the deliciously formidable ruler of Riseholme's social world. Her battles for cultural supremacy with her neighbors are comedy of the highest order. The first of Benson's beloved Lucia novels, and a perfect satire of pretension.
in-times-of-peril-a-tale-of-india: Henty's tale of the Indian Mutiny follows a brave boy through the siege of Lucknow and the perils of 1857. Daring escapes, loyal friends, and British pluck fill these exciting pages. The Mutiny as Henty's young readers thrilled to it, vividly told.
the-captivi-and-the-mostellaria: Plautus, the great Roman comic, offers The Captivi and The Mostellaria — prisoners and haunted houses turned to laughter. His robust farce delighted Rome and inspires still. Ancient comedy at its liveliest. Slaves outwit masters in these robust Roman farces, fresh as ever.
old-calabria: Norman Douglas explores Old Calabria — Italy's wild toe, its brigands, saints, and ancient ruins. His learned, witty travelogue is a classic. The Mediterranean as only Douglas saw it. Greek temples, bandit caves, and peasant shrines crowd his learned tour. Few travel books wear their learning so lightly.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abecedaria: A 1913 entry on abecedaria — early alphabets scratched on stone and wall by ancient schoolboys. Henri Leclercq, the great archaeologist, gathers the evidence. Children's lessons from two thousand years ago. Charming relics of old schools. Catacomb walls still show the children's careful letters.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abyssinia: This 1913 reference piece on Abyssinia — Ethiopia, the ancient Christian empire. Jean-Baptiste Piolet tells of its kings and monks. The eunuch's baptism began its faith. Africa's oldest Christian land. Lalibela's rock churches amaze travelers still. Its monks kept the faith through Muslim sieges.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acacia: A 1913 entry on the acacia — the shittim wood of the tabernacle and ark. Anthony Maas traces it through Scripture. Desert timber for a holy house. Botany in the service of the Bible. Its thorns crown the desert traveler's path. The ark's boards were cut from its wood.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acadia: A 1913 entry on Acadia — the French colony of the Maritimes, and its Catholic story. Thomas Campbell tells of settlers and exiles. The Grand Dérangement scattered its people. Longfellow's Evangeline keeps their memory. The Cajuns of Louisiana descend from its exiles.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achaia: This 1913 reference piece on Achaia — the Roman province of Paul's Greek mission. Wendell Reilly maps its cities and proconsuls. Corinth and Athens heard the apostle. The Gospel's Greek beachhead. Gallio judged Paul before its tribunal. The province gave the Church its first Greek saints.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acmonia: This 1913 reference article on Acmonia — the Phrygian town, now a titular see. Its bishops' names survive in old lists. Asia Minor's forgotten Christianity. A name kept alive in the hierarchy. Its coins show the city's ancient pride. Paul may have passed its gates.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acolouthia: This 1913 reference piece on the acolouthia — the order of the Byzantine divine office. John Goggin explains its structure. Vespers, matins, and hours in solemn train. The East's liturgy, methodically set. Its books fill the monastery libraries. Every feast has its proper order.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-actus-et-pote: This 1913 reference article on actus et potentia — act and potency, the poles of scholastic metaphysics. Charles Dubray explains the great distinction. All change is potency becoming act. Aristotle's key, in Aquinas' hand.
